minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  April 20, 2021

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  April 20, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Council Member Morales
  announced the call-in instructions for public comments.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at 2:04 p.m.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at 2:05 p.m.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agendas.

  Wanda York called and asked if she could comment on the citywide parking.

  Mayor Butts encouraged the caller to wait toward the ending of the City Council Meeting
  to address her concerns during open public comments.

  Mayor Butts called the City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and
  Housing Authority at the hour of 2:09 p.m.

  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.

  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April
  15, 2021, in the amount of $2,160,316.67 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority is hereby authorized to certify
  upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  1
 April 20, 2021

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Padilla that the Minutes for the Council Meetings held on August 25, 2020, and
  September 1, 2020, be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None; and
  Abstain: Council Member Faulk.

  101  AGREEMENT NO. 21-143 APPROVED – GRIFFIN STRUCTURES, INC.;
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-80 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-
  2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated April 20, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval of an agreement with Griffin Structures, Inc. to provide construction
  management services for the Emergency Operations Center (EOC).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-143 in an amount not
  to exceed $177,600; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-80 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2021-2022 ANNUAL
  BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  AGREEMENT NO. 21-144 APPROVED – LPA, INC.; RESOLUTION NO. 21-81
  ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-2021 BUDGET. Staff report
  dated April 20, 2021, was presented recommending approval of an agreement with LPA,
  Inc. to provide architectural services for the Emergency Operations Center (EOC).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-143 in an amount not
  to exceed $107,640; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-81 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2021-2022 ANNUAL
  BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  INGLEWOOD GROWING ARTISTS PROJECT (IGAP) 2020 RECEIVED AND
  FILED. Staff report dated April 20, 2021, recommending receiving and filing the
  Inglewood Growing Artists Project (IGAP) 2020, which provides for the purchase and
  installation of the “Love, Inglewood” Collection: 13 original artworks on paper by
  Inglewood artists, in an amount no to exceed $20,000.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby receive and file the Inglewood Growing Artist Project
  2020. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 4 TO MOU P00F3128 APPROVED – LACMTA; MAYOR
  AUTHORIZED – EXECUTION OF AMENDMENT NO. 4 ON BEHALF OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD. Staff report dated April 20 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of Amendment No. 4 to MOU P00F3128 with LACMTA to
  extend the lapsing date of the Century Boulevard Mobility Improvement Project to
  February 28, 2022.

  2
 April 20, 2021

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 4 to MOU P00F3128;
  and 2) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 4 on behalf of the City of
  Inglewood. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO AGREEMENT 16-157 APPROVED – WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING. Staff report dated April 20, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval of Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. 16-157 with Willdan Engineering to
  extend the Term of the Agreement by up to 90 days.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. 16-157.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO AGREEMENT NO. 16-016 APPROVED – PSOMAS:
  RESOLUTION NO. 21-82 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2020-
  2021 CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM (CIP) BUDGET. Staff report dated
  April 20 2021, was presented recommending approval of Amendment No. 3 to
  Agreement No. 16-016 (Agreement) with PSOMAS (Consultant) extending the term of
  the Agreement for five (5) additional months and increasing the compensation in an
  additional amount of $59,824 (new total contract amount not to exceed $5,313,512).

  It was moved by Council/Successor Agency Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council/Successor Agency Member Faulk that the City Council/Successor Agency does
  hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. 16-016; and 2) Adopt
  Resolution No. 21-82 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD AMENDING THE 2020-2021, ANNUAL BUDGET TO
  PROVIDE  FUNDING  FOR  CONSTRUCTION  CONTRACT
  ADMINISTRATION THROUGH PROJECT CLOSE-OUT AND TO ASSIST
  THE PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT WITH RESOLVING ANY
  POTENTIAL CONSTRUCTION CLAIMS AND DISPUTES.

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk,
  and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke on Brown Act Violations. She also requested returned
  phone calls and emails.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke concerning issues with access to the City Council Meetings
  and the reading of George Floyd's verdict, which causes the City to respond in a case of
  emergency.

  Wanda York spoke concerning the citywide parking permit program. She also felt the
  City was making a mistake requiring a parking permit because it only allows 12 passes
  per quarter. She also disagreed with submitting her driver's license to obtain a permit.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the honor of Sargent Juan Ferreira at the hour of 2:19 p.m.
